The Taliban decided not to parade captured American military hardware on 15 August this year so as not to annoy US president Donald Trump, according to experts monitoring the subdued anniversary celebrations in Kabul.

Previous propaganda displays to mark what the Taliban call “Victory Day” – when hardline militants seized control of the country on 15 August 2021 – have included a show of force involving captured American tanks and Humvees at the former US-run Bagram air base north of the capital.

The historic Soviet-built airstrip was the main base for American forces following the invasion after 9/11. The size of a small city, its capture by the Taliban shortly after it was vacated by the US was a hugely symbolic moment during the withdrawal of Nato forces.

The largest grand parade held by the Taliban at Bagram was in 2024. It hosted an audience of nearly 10,000 men, including the Taliban’s acting defence minister Mullah Yaqoob and acting interior minister Sirajuddin Haqqani. It also invited senior diplomats from China and Russia, who were seen in attendance as American Humvees and M4 tanks rolled out on the tarmac.

The Taliban executed the grand parade on the two runways and over 100 parking spots for fighter jets – known as revetments for the blast walls which protect each aircraft. One of the runways, built in 2006, measures more than 12,000ft long. The air base also boasts a passenger lounge, a 50-bed hospital and hangar-sized tents filled with furniture.

Leaders of the regime made speeches aimed at an international audience, urging the diaspora to return and for the West to interact and cooperate with the country’s rulers.

In February this year, Mr Trump said it “makes him angry” to see the Taliban displaying American vehicles and equipment and “run them up on a little street”.

open image in gallery A convoy of Taliban security personnel take part in a parade in front of the former US Embassy building (back) in Kabul ( AFP/Getty )

"We left a lot of it, although a lot of it, but very small, relatively, in Afghanistan. The Taliban has it. You know, they have their parade every year where they take our military vehicles and run them up some little street, and like it's their form of a military parade, and it makes me angry when I see that. Angry. When I see that, I get angry," the US president said.

David S Sedney, a senior commentator on US-Afghanistan ties, tellsThe Independent: “They didn't have that Bagram parade or celebration this year, and I think it's a reasonable analysis to say that was not necessarily a signal to Trump, but it was an effort not to make Trump more angry.”

"It wasn't a signal of reaching out. It was just a decision: 'We don't want to make Trump even more angry' because they've seen Trump... can act very illogically, and so they don't want to anger him. They didn't want to tick him off, but they still had to have a parade,” Mr Sedney, who served as the former deputy assistant secretary of defence for Afghanistan in the first cabinet of the Obama administration, said.

open image in gallery US president Donald Trump speaks to the troops during a surprise Thanksgiving day visit at Bagram Air Field in 2019 ( AFP via Getty Images )

Hundreds of American Humvees have been left to rust in scrapyards across Afghanistan, five years after the US abandoned the trucks – so emblematic of its military campaign in the country – to the new Taliban regime. Satellite images from former Nato and US bases in several Afghan provinces show the US-made vehicles dismantled and hollowed out, with their parts haphazardly strewn around open-air garages and compounds.

The US forces tried to dismantle or destroy much of their machinery, from aircraft to computer systems, in the last weeks of their chaotic pull-out from Afghanistan after 20 years of war. But much still fell to the Taliban in August 2021 when the US-trained Afghan military crumbled and surrendered to the Islamist militants, according to US defence officials.

A senior spokesperson for the Taliban’s Islamic Emirate, Abdul Qahar Balkhi, said the weapons and military equipment left behind in Afghanistan belonged to the group and will remain under their control, with no chance of it being returned to the US.

open image in gallery An aerial view of the landscape outside of Bagram Air Field is seen in Bagram, Afghanistan ( Getty Images )

In September last year, Mr Trump said he was negotiating with the Taliban to retake control of the Bagram airbase in Afghanistan.

“We want that base back,” he said, calling it one of the biggest airbases in the world. “One of the reasons we want the [Bagram] base back is because it is an hour away from where China makes its nuclear weapons. So a lot of things are happening,” he said.

Zabiullah Mujahid, the Taliban’s spokesperson, had dismissed these remarks from Mr Trump as “emotional” and said US officials should “refrain” from making “statements based on unsubstantiated information”.

open image in gallery A convoy of Taliban security personnel take part in a parade in front of the former US Embassy building in Kabul ( AFP/Getty )

Though there was no parade at Bagram this year, the US’s former presence in Afghanistan still featured in a rather more muted celebration, as Taliban fighters drove armoured vehicles past the former US embassy building in Kabul, displaying flags and banners declaring victory over American forces. Convoys of vehicles wound their way through the city, causing traffic jams.

"This is the street in front of the American embassy. It was heavily fortified with a massive security presence,” said Mr Sedney. “The Taliban have removed that and it is back the way it was 20 years ago. You can drive up and down it, and they had a parade, and they had several thousands of people lining the sides of that road, and the parade was of [the Taliban’s] ministry of interior vehicles and troops.”

open image in gallery A boy holds an AK-style rifle while sitting in a vehicle decorated with Taliban flags during celebrations marking the fifth anniversary of the US withdrawal from Afghanistan and the Taliban's return to power in Kabul ( AP )

The parade was led by Sirajuddin Haqqani, the Taliban’s interim interior minister who leads a powerful faction within the Taliban and is reported to be at odds with the ageing supreme leader Akhundzada in Kandahar.

“Sirajuddin Haqqani had a pretty nice little parade in a very symbolic area because it was right in front of the US embassy. That's actually much more insulting to the US than Bagram. They chose to do it. It was very clear,” Mr Sedney said.

open image in gallery The former US Embassy building is pictured during a parade by Taliban security personnel celebrating the fifth anniversary of their return to power in Kabul ( AFP/Getty )

A video shared by the Taliban’s interior ministry of the celebrations from inside the US embassy were similar to the 2021 celebrations when the Taliban fighters entered the presidential palace.

“They showed empty desks and places I've been to... So they were showing 'we have control of your embassy,' and then outside they were doing a victory parade saying 'we beat you'," he said.

Asif Durrani, the former Pakistan ambassador to Iran, says the Taliban cannot help but hark back to their defeat of the American enemy, even at a time when they are courting greater acceptance from the international community and normalised relations with the US.

open image in gallery A convoy of Taliban security personnel take part in a parade in front of the former US Embassy building in Kabul ( AFP/Getty )

“The Taliban lack the art of governance; therefore, whatever they did [as de facto authorities of Kabul] did not impact them domestically or abroad. Unfortunately, Afghan history is replete with such idiosyncratic practices where the ‘victor or vanquished’ psyche ruled the roost. That psyche still prevails,” Pakistan’s senior diplomat and former special representative to Afghanistan told The Independent, on the celebrations in Kabul.

Ultimately, it is a testament to Afghanistan’s pariah status that however it chooses to mark its victory will have little impact on either its neighbours or the US, Mr Durrani says. “What kind of victory parade is that, for an entity facing global isolation?”

News.title: Karmelo Anthony backed out of testifying over concerns of damaging evidence
News.content:
The latest headlines from our reporters across the US sent straight to your inbox each weekday Your briefing on the latest headlines from across the US Your briefing on the latest headlines from across the US Email * SIGN UP I would like to be emailed about offers, events and updates from The Independent. Read our Privacy notice

Karmelo Anthony had planned to testify at his Texas murder trial over the fatal stabbing at a high school track meet but ultimately decided against it after concerns emerged that prosecutors could introduce potentially damaging evidence about his past, one of his attorneys said Friday.

Anthony, 19, is seeking a new trial after a jury in June sentenced him to 35 years in prison for killing 17-year-old Austin Metcalf, a student at a rival school who was stabbed during a confrontation at a track competition last year. The case has since heightened racial tensions, with both families becoming targets of harrassment.

On the second day of a hearing near Dallas, defense attorney Toby Shook said Anthony’s plans to testify fell apart over fears that prosecutors could break agreements not to introduce evidence that might further inflame the already highly charged case.

open image in gallery During the trial, lawyers on both sides told jurors the tragedy had nothing to do with race ( Texas Department of Criminal Justice )

“It was essential that the jury hear Karmelo and hear his explanation,” Shook said.

It was not clear when state District Judge Michael Chitty would issue a ruling on whether to grant a new trial.

Prosecutor Bill Wirskye has defended the trial as fair and said the possibility of Anthony testifying wasn't part of the original agreement with the defense. Anthony's attorneys say it should have been obvious the teenager would want to explain to jurors himself how he acted in self-defense.

Anthony is Black; Metcalf was white. Among the details that jurors never heard, according to attorneys on both sides, were that Anthony once sent a text message fantasizing about stabbing someone and Metcalf had a history of fighting and using racist language.

During the trial, lawyers on both sides told jurors the tragedy had nothing to do with race, but social media posts amplified the killing nationwide in racial terms.

In an interview with NewsNation, Metcalf's father, Jeff Metcalf, said he supported the original agreement between prosecutors and defense attorneys. He said information about his son's juvenile history does not change what happened the day his son was killed.

open image in gallery Anthony's attorneys have also told the judge he should get a new trial because of errors that limited access to the proceedings. ( Pat Lopez via AP )

“We all want our children to be the best they can be, and obviously, we all fall short,” Jeff Metcalf told NewsNation. “It still doesn’t change the facts of the case.”

Metcalf's parents and Anthony's parents have attended both days of the hearing.

Anthony's attorneys have also told the judge he should get a new trial because of errors that limited access to the proceedings. They have argued that the case’s original judge allowed a “shadow docket” that shielded character information about both sides.

The trial in June took place amid heightened court security. Wirskye said there had been threats against a judge who granted Anthony bond, fake autopsy reports circulating online and attempts to intimidate witnesses. Parents of some witnesses also filed protective orders for their children because of threats, according to Wirskye.

Anthony secured one legal victory this week when the judge who presided over his trial was removed from the case. Chitty was then assigned to consider the motion for a retrial.

Anthony’s attorneys had asked for state District Judge John Roach to be removed in part because of a TV interview in which Roach said jurors “got it right” when they delivered a guilty verdict.

News.title: Arsenal play like the champions they are as title defence starts with a bang
News.content:
Good evening and welcome to the Emirates Stadium, where the Premier League champions begin the defence of their title. Or, as Mikel Arteta prefers to put it, their “attack” on a new season. A classic Arteta-ism.

The assault starts tonight against Coventry City but our understanding is that Arsenal will be without new £75m midfielder Bruno Guimaraes. We believe the Brazilian has picked up an injury, and it’s not currently clear how severe it might be. Clearly, this is a blow for Arteta. But they should still have enough to get past promoted Coventry… shouldn’t they? We’ll find out soon enough.

Meanwhile, Arteta has said he and his players should relish being Premier League title favourites and the role of the hunted rather than the hunter.

“In the last three seasons, at some point we were first and at some point we were chasing. And you never know what is better,” Arteta said. “But if you give me the choice, I want to be first. I want to be hunted, and I want to be in control of our future, rather than depending on somebody else.”

Arteta called on his players to retain the hunger they had last season.

“We start from scratch, from zero, and we’re going to have to prove we are at the level to go back to that position again,” he said. “We need to show that desire and the ambition to be better than what we were last season, a month ago, a week ago.”

This is Coventry’s first Premier League campaign since they suffered relegation in 2000-01, and they were led to the Championship title by Frank Lampard. They scored the most goals in the Championship and conceded the fewest, and could face one of their former players tonight in Viktor Gyokeres.

Full team news as and when we get it.

News.title: Russell takes Dutch GP sprint pole as Antonelli struggles to fifth
News.content:
Welcome to our live coverage for sprint qualifying for the 2026 Dutch Grand Prix from Zandvoort. This is the last time the race will be on the F1 calendar for the foreseeable future, having been reintroduced in 2021 after a 35-year absence. It will be a shame to see it leave again, but never rule out it coming back, especially with Max Verstappen signing a lengthy contract extension with Red Bull.

What of the competitive action this weekend? As it is a sprint weekend, there is not a lot of preparation time, with just one practice session before sprint qualifying. In that it was a fairly close fight at the top, and it was Kimi Antonelli, the championship leader, who was fastest of all. Behind him was the McLaren of Lando Norris who was 0.121sec adrift then George Russell, who will be looking to kickstart his title campaign here, a further 0.004sec behind him.

Then came the two Ferraris of Lewis Hamilton (0.190sec) and Charles Leclerc (0.289sec) before a fairly significant gap of 0.659sec to Oscar Piastri in sixth. Verstappen was down in 11th, nearly 1.4sec off Antonelli’s ultimate pace but 0.5sec or so ahead of new (and old) team-mate for the weekend, Liam Lawson.

It was a tricky session for the drivers, though, as it began damp on a showery and blustery day by the Dutch seaside. Several drivers ran wide and off the track, though they all avoided anything more serious than gravel rash. The rest of the day looks to be drier but there are still a few showers around and the wind is all over the place, as it often is here.

Sprint qualifying starts at 3.30pm BST and we will be here for all of the updates for the nearly hour-long session.

News.title: Root delivers perfect riposte to captaincy doubters as England hammer Pakistan
News.content:
There was no attempt to be a Ben Stokes tribute act by Joe Root, just a measured captaincy performance very much in his own undemonstrative style.

Root, ever the team man, pushed his bowlers forward to lead England off at the end, recognising the match-winners in a walkover against Pakistan, who were bowled out for 135 in under two sessions.

Victory by an innings and 103 runs inside three days marked a perfect return to the job and put the smile back on England faces for the first time in a long while. The chants of “F--- the ECB” from Trent Bridge, after the New Zealand regime-toppling loss, were replaced by the Yorkshire faithful’s “Roooot”.

There was plenty of scepticism around rebooting the Root captaincy, but he was the only realistic choice. Harry Brook’s batting here was more sensible and at a tempo in the captain’s mould. “He is still learning the art of Test cricket,” Root said. Thrusting Brook into the job would have put more pressure on him, he may well have felt he needed to make risky statements with the bat. Now he can mature under Root and Stephen Fleming.

Tactically, Root was astute and showed enough to suggest he is going to be different this time. The old Root would not have whipped Jofra Archer off after two overs of the Test, but it was a prod that worked as he bowled quicker and more accurately to strike twice with the second-innings new ball, using his new-found skills with a scrambled seam to good effect.

It also showed his bowlers he wanted a fuller length and, from that first hour, they controlled the match and did not let their grip slip.

Root promised to keep the good aspects of Bazball and apply common sense. He continued Stokes’s leg-slip tactic and it paid off with the wicket of opener Azan Awais, and urged Ollie Robinson to bowl with the keeper standing up. England batted at 4.5 an over – a touch quicker than the Bazball years – but it was never reckless, just a calm tempo, with no ramps or scoops.

News.title: Officials selling yellow fever certificates to unvaccinated travellers
News.content:
Officials in Malawi are selling yellow fever certificates to unvaccinated travellers for around $20 and sending them on their way, a Telegraph investigation has found.



The passport-sized, yellow document, officially called the International Certificate of Vaccination or Prophylaxis (ICVP), is supposed to provide proof of vaccination against yellow fever, a mosquito-borne virus that kills tens of thousands of people every year.

The jab provides lifelong protection, beginning 10 days after vaccination. Most countries in Africa and Latin America require them for entry, either for all travellers or for those arriving from risk areas.



Yet travellers leaving Malawi through two major airports can get hold of the certificates without ever being vaccinated, according to interviews with multiple travellers and an undercover investigation.



Several passengers who travelled recently from Malawi to destinations including Uganda, Kenya, Ethiopia and China said they had obtained yellow fever vaccination certificates at airports or public hospitals without receiving the vaccine.



One traveller, who recently flew to Uganda for work from Kamuzu International Airport, which serves the capital, Lilongwe, said he was initially told it was too late to get vaccinated because his departure was less than 10 days away.



“When I asked the health officials if I could get vaccinated at the airport, I was told it was too late because I needed to be vaccinated ten days before my trip,” he told The Telegraph.



“But then they offered to arrange the certificate for me for roughly $21,” said the traveller, who asked not to be named. “I had to pay because I could not postpone the trip.”

News.title: Congo gambles on ‘old’ vaccine as new Ebola virus spirals
News.content:
Nearly half of all those infected have gone on to die.

Dr Sania Nishtar, chief executive of the Gavi global vaccine partnership, earlier this week said to beat the outbreak “we must deploy every tool at our disposal”.

She went on: “To avoid this becoming the worst recorded Ebola outbreak in history, it is critical that all effective countermeasure options are brought to bear.

“We have a tool that could help save lives while we wait for [Bundibugyo]-specific vaccines to become available.”

Previous clinical trials have shown that Ervebo is safe, but its effect on other strains is unknown.

The World Health Organisation said in a statement that while it was not known if Ervebo may protect against the Bundibugyo virus, “early laboratory and animal data suggest it may provide some protection”.

Medics told the Telegraph of anecdotal claims that health workers who had been given Ervebo to protect them during an outbreak of the Zaire strain in 2018 to 2020 had not fallen ill during the current Bundibugyo outbreak.

Health workers are at extreme risk of catching the disease because they come into contact with highly-contagious blood, vomit and diarrhoea from dying patients. When they fall sick themselves, they frequently go on to infect their own families.

Giving health workers vaccine jabs to protect them as they tend the sick is a cornerstone of Ebola responses.

The WHO said the vaccine allocation includes 20,000 doses for a Phase 3 clinical trial to understand the impact of the vaccine on the Bundibugyo virus. The remaining 50,000 doses will be used for front-line and health workers as recommended by WHO experts.

Dr Nishtar said: “Having already been licensed for the Zaire strain, we know that Ervebo is proven to be safe.

“And while the signs are that it may not stop transmission – which is essential for ending the outbreak - it could well save precious lives and reduce suffering.”

Health officials warn that the Bundibugyo outbreak centred on DRC’s Ituri province is easily outpacing relief efforts.

The virus is thought to have been spreading for months before an outbreak was finally declared in mid-May and medics have been unable to make up the head start.

An analysis by the Africa Centres for Disease Control meanwhile warned the current outbreak dwarfed all others on record

The current outbreak had almost ten times more cases than any other previous outbreak at a similar stage.

News.title: Soaring welfare bill pushes national debt to almost £3tn
News.content:
Britain’s soaring welfare bill forced John Healey to borrow more to balance the books last month.

The gap between tax receipts and spending unexpectedly resulted in a £1.8bn deficit in July, taking the national debt to within a whisker of £3tn.

Economists had predicted the Government would borrow nothing and blamed the deficit on the rising welfare bill.

Figures published by the Office for National Statistics (ONS) this morning show total debt rose to £2.985tn in July.

Benefit payments also climbed by 7.2pc, or £2bn, to £30bn last month.

The Chancellor now faces another tax-raising Budget in October, even as strong receipts from self-employed workers provide some respite.

The ONS also said Mr Healey spent £7.7bn on debt interest in July alone, almost 10pc higher than a year ago.

Ashley Webb, at Capital Economics said: “The weak performance was mainly due higher social payments.”

Monthly borrowing was slightly higher than the Office for Budget Responsibility and markets expected, meaning the Government has borrowed £56.7bn this financial year to plug the gap between tax receipts and public spending.

Julian Jessop, an independent economist and IEA economics fellow, said: “The latest official data highlight the fragility of the public finances as John Healey prepares his first Budget. Government borrowing was £2.3bn above forecast in July, and £0.7bn higher than in the same month a year ago.”

July is traditionally a strong month for receipts from the self-employed, with self-assessed income tax receipts last month coming to £17.1bn, about £1.7bn more than a year earlier.

However, higher inflation triggered by the Iran war means Mr Healey will be forced to use the Budget to find billions of pounds to repair the public finances.

Mr Healey said: “Fiscal discipline is the bedrock of our UK economic stability and national security which is why we are committed to meeting our fiscal rules, with a buffer against global uncertainties.”

The Resolution Foundation warned that the Chancellor’s headroom against his fiscal rules - self-imposed guardrails to guide public spending - has shrunk from around £24bn in the Spring Statement to less than £8bn today.

The think tank called on the Chancellor to use his first Budget on Oct 28 to put the nation’s finances on a more sustainable path.

Elliott Christensen, senior economist at the Resolution Foundation, said: “The Chancellor’s margin against his fiscal rules is now razor thin.”

News.title: Brook falls agonisingly short of Headingley hundred again as England continue to dominate
News.content:
“Yeah, of course I did,” said Cox, when asked if he was frustrated to miss out on three figures. Cox was caught behind off spinner Ali Usman, but believed he had hit his pad with his bat, not the ball.

“Once I got to fifty, I moved to sixty quickly, and thought ‘there’s a chance here’. Just keep being disciplined, ball by ball. I had it at the back of my mind, thinking you have worked so hard, do not give this opportunity up. That is exactly what I do in county cricket. I get to fifty, see how many runs I need to score, and work down from there.”

Asked if his team-mates were feeling the same emotion, he said: “Oh yeah there is. Every team, every player wants to score Test hundreds. Four of us got fifties, so we were hoping one would kick on, and instead of making it just a hundred, make it 150 or 170.

“I am thrilled. I would have taken it at the start of the Test match. I let myself down a tiny bit, but at the end of the day, you take 70.”

Cox resumed on day two on 23, then was dropped by the bowler Khurram Shahzad on 57. In the course of his innings, he was compared to AB de Villiers by the former England captain Michael Vaughan.

Cox is likely to get a good run across formats. England had hoped to call on Sam Curran for the third Test of this series, but his summer is over due to a groin injury. Curran will undergo surgery on Friday.

It is likely England will be without Curran, Bethell and Tom Banton for September’s white-ball series against Sri Lanka, which should mean greater opportunity for the likes of Cox and Sussex’s James Coles, and could even see a recall for Zak Crawley, who made an assured 81 for Kent against Middlesex on Thursday. Will Jacks is currently sidelined with appendicitis, but is expected to have recovered in time for the series.

Sports.title: Man Utd news: Next signing after Carlos Baleba decided as Myles Lewis-Skelly verdict reached
Sports.content:
Man Utd news: Next signing after Carlos Baleba decided as Myles Lewis-Skelly verdict reached

As Manchester United prepare for their Premier League opener, there is still time for Michael Carrick to add to his squad

View 2 Images Carlos Baleba might not be the last signing to join Manchester United this summer (Image: Mike Hewitt/Getty Images)

The wait is over for Manchester United fans. No, not for their latest transfer, but rather for their first Premier League action of the new season.

‌



Another addition might not be too far away, though. Michael Carrick won't have Carlos Baleba in his squad in time for Saturday's lunchtime kick-off against Hull City but progress is being made on a deal for the Brighton star.

‌



Baleba looks set to join Andrey Santos and Youri Tielemans among United's midfield options and the Cameroonian might not be the last new addition. There's still more than a week to get deals done and that leaves time for plenty of movement.

‌



We've also got an update on Myles Lewis-Skelly, whose name has been mentioned in connection with a United switch this summer. Here are our latest lines from around Old Trafford.

FOLLOW OUR MAN UTD FB PAGE! Latest United news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Coleen Rooney beams with joy as she reveals Man Utd starlet son Kai's GCSE results READ MORE :

Next move after Baleba

United are expected to explore a move for a new left-back once they have completed their move for Carlos Baleba, according to the Manchester Evening News. There are still some final touches to be made to the Baleba deal but soon attentions can be turned elsewhere.

‌



Luke Shaw remains United's first choice in the position but the extra toll of Champions League football means there may well be a desire for someone who can provide immediate competition and the quality to succeed the England international in the long-term.

View 2 Images Alejandro Balde is among the left-backs to be linked with an Old Trafford switch (Image: Urbanandsport/NurPhoto/Shutterstock)

Lewis Hall and Jorge Salinas have both emerged as potential targets, while reports in Spain have also pointed to interest in Alejandro Balde of Barcelona. However, unless Newcastle can be convinced to change their hard stance on Hall, United might have to wait for the former Chelsea star.

Arteta sends Lewis-Skelly message

Mikel Arteta said Myles Lewis-Skelly will "100 per cent" still be an Arsenal player when the transfer window shuts. The comments appear to draw a line under any hopes of a United or Chelsea move for the 19-year-old.

"The players that have been raised in our system, and they feel generally that love and that connection with the club, bring something else, there's no question about that," the manager added. "We need to look after them in a really special way because they bring value that is very difficult to find.

Sports.title: Arsenal news: Mikel Arteta ‘closing in’ on trio as Julian Alvarez transfer twist emerges
Sports.content:
Arsenal news: Mikel Arteta ‘closing in’ on trio as Julian Alvarez transfer twist emerges

Arsenal have been linked with several targets in the summer transfer window, including Atletico Madrid's Julian Alvarez

View 2 Images Arsenal have been linked with a move for Julian Alvarez (Image: Eduardo Carmim/Eurasia Sport Images/Getty Images)

Arsenal are continuing to work on strengthening their squad ahead of transfer deadline day on September 1. Mikel Arteta is focused on helping the club retain the Premier League after guiding the club to their first league title in 22 years.

The Gunners are recruiting from a formidable position of strength, signing former Newcastle United captain Bruno Guimaraes in midfield and bolstering their wide options with Christos Tzolis. Arsenal have also completed the signing of England centre-back Ezri Konsa from Aston Villa.

While the majority of the club’s summer recruits should have an immediate impact on Arteta’s team, the Gunners have also shown signs of long-term planning. Arsenal are reportedly targeting a trio of prospects who could become future stars at the Emirates Stadium.

Meanwhile, the Gunners have been heavily linked with a marquee move for Atletico Madrid forward Julian Alvarez throughout the summer. Here, Mirror Football looks at some of the biggest transfer stories surrounding the club.

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

Arsenal ‘closing in’ on trio

Arsenal are reportedly nearing a deal for Blackburn Rovers striker Igor Tyjon. The 18-year-old forward is one of three young prospects considered close to joining the club.

Julian Alvarez to Arsenal twist as huge transfer agreement wrecks forward's dream move READ MORE :

Sergio Aguero names surprise rival for Arsenal retaining Premier League title READ MORE :

The Evening Standard reports that Arteta’s side are closing in on a move for Tyjon worth an initial £1million, with another £2m in possible add-ons. The teenager, who was scheduled for a medical on Friday, has been a long-standing target for Arsenal.

Tyjon has reportedly rejected a professional contract at Blackburn, where he has made three first team appearances, and is expected to join Arsenal’s U21 squad, though he will link up with Arteta’s side in first team training. The young forward could also be joined by two Manchester United prospects at the north London club.

The Evening Standard states that United defender Habeeb Ogunneye, 20, has undergone a medical ahead of joining Arsenal’s U21s and training with the senior team. United winger James Scanlon is also nearing a move to the Gunners from Old Trafford.

View 2 Images Blackburn Rovers' Igor Tyjon is reportedly nearing a move to Arsenal (Image: Trevor Wilkinson | MI News/NurPhoto via Getty Images)

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

Julian Alvarez transfer stance changes

Meanwhile, Atletico Madrid are claimed to have softened their stance on the prospect of Julian Alvarez leaving the club. The Argentine forward has been linked with a move to Arsenal, who reportedly held a meeting in London with Atleti director Mateu Alemany to discuss a possible deal.

Spanish publication Mundo Deportivo reports that Atleti have “agreed” to enter negotiations with Arsenal over a move for Alvarez, marking a shift in the club’s stance. However, it is added that the La Liga side have been “very clear” about their unwillingness to discuss a potential deal with Barcelona.

Alvarez has publicly discussed his desire to leave Atleti this season but is reportedly “not keen” on a move to Arsenal, despite the club’s change of stance, and still prefers Barcelona.

Given the little time Atleti have to find a replacement, Arsenal’s Viktor Gyokeres is mentioned as a potential solution. However, Alvarez’s situation is described as “untenable” with the former Manchester City star refusing to return to the Premier League.

Sports.title: Roberto De Zerbi convinced Tottenham can challenge for the title after spending spree
Sports.content:
Roberto De Zerbi convinced Tottenham can challenge for the title after spending spree

Roberto De Zerbi believes Tottenham can go from relegation candidates to title challengers after a productive summer transfer window, which has seen them splash the cash

View 3 Images Roberto De Zerbi is very optimistic of Spurs' chances this season (Image: Marc Atkins/Getty Images)

Roberto De Zerbi believes Tottenham have “big potential” to challenge for the title.

De Zerbi insisted he will not know whether his new-look squad are the real deal until after the transfer window shuts. But after a huge spending spree, which is set to go over £300million with the arrival of Manchester City pair Savinho and Omar Marmoush, the Spurs boss insists they have got the quality to be genuine challengers.

That would be a huge leap from finishing 17th in each of the last two seasons but De Zerbi is full of optimism after a huge summer. De Zerbi said: “Big potential. At the end of the transfer market, I will be more accurate in my opinion.

“Maybe we will know now. Maybe we have to see on the pitch. To be honest everyone we are very excited but in the end the pitch speaks, as we say in Italian. If we start now with big words, I love pressure. It's not a problem of pressure, but if we are to be honest and correct, we have to wait for the answer from the pitch.

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

“Football is a connection. Football is like magic. You can sometimes find the connection between players when every player thinks like the coach or we come together with an idea of football and the players who don’t start in the team are the biggest fans of the players who are playing. We have to create something on the pitch and off the pitch to compete like we want.”

De Zerbi insists the club’s first £100m player, Italy midfielder Sandro Tonali, is even better than he realised and they have broken the bank to bring in Mateus Fernandes as well as John Paul van Hecke to bolster the squad.

This week De Zerbi insisted he was aiming to reach the top and, while he was wary of setting targets, he admitted the team is now getting close to what he wants. De Zerbi said: “On paper its very close. On the pitch we have to see and we have to work. I am experienced enough not to say too much. I’m very happy with the squad.

View 3 Images Sandro Tonali is the most expensive of Tottenham's summer signings (Image: Getty Images)

“We have to complete the squad but at the moment I am very happy. The answer I receive from the pitch has to be like my dreams and my thoughts with the board. I have to keep the balance because sometimes the transfer market - with Tonali and JP Van Hecke - we bring in a lot.

“But if we have to push then I will be the first to push, to fix the target higher but now is not the right moment. Now is the moment to think about Brentford and to complete the transfer market. Then we can fix what target you want without arrogance but also with big ambitions because this is Tottenham, not another smaller team.”

De Zerbi joked that the past three months of rebuild have felt more like “10 years” but also stressed the near miss of relegation last season must serve as a reminder.

They have named not just one new captain after Cristian Romero’s departure, but five with Micky van de Ven, Pedro Porro, Ben Davies, James Maddison and Archie Gray in a leadership group. Van de Ven will wear the armband when fit.

View 3 Images Jan Paul van Hecke is another new arrival at Tottenham (Image: Marc Atkins/Getty Images)

De Zerbi added: “I think we can't forget what happened last season. It's a lesson, a big lesson for us, for every one of us. But anyway, we have to go on another page and to start another season, an important season.

“We are building, I think, a new project. And now the big challenge, without talking too much about the target, the goal of this season, the first two targets we have very clear in ourselves is to find the soul of the team.

“And the second target: to improve in our organisation of football. With the ball, without the ball, our style has to be the key of our season, like our soul. These two characteristics I want to find as soon as possible.”

Sports.title: Carlos Baleba to Man Utd transfer details as medical set after breakthrough in Brighton talks
Sports.content:
Carlos Baleba to Man Utd transfer details as medical set after breakthrough in Brighton talks

Manchester United have a full agreement with Brighton over the signing of midfielder Carlos Baleba, who will travel this weekend to undergo a medical

View 2 Images Carlos Baleba is heading to Manchester United (Image: Photo by Mike Hewitt/Getty Images)

Manchester United are poised to sign Carlos Baleba after Brighton agreed a fee and gave him the green light to travel for a medical on Saturday.

‌



United have been interested in Baleba for over a year and now have a deal in place for the 22-year-old midfielder. After seeing an initial offer of £60million plus £5m in add-ons rejected, the two clubs have shaken hands on £65m plus £5m in add-ons, reports the Manchester Evening News, with a sell-on clause also included in the deal.

‌



Youri Tielemans and Andrey Santos have already joined United this summer for a combined total of £85m, but manager Michael Carrick has always wanted a third player. United first enquired about Baleba last summer, only to be put off by Brighton's £100m asking price for the Cameroon international.

‌



A much lower-key 2025/26 campaign has seen his value decrease and United have moved to secure his services, having already agreed personal terms. He will travel up to Manchester this weekend and become their fourth major signing this summer, after Tielemans, Santos and Karl Darlow.

FOLLOW OUR MAN UTD FB PAGE! Latest United news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

‌



Baleba will have to wait for his United debut, however, after picking up an ankle ligament injury during Brighton's 0-0 draw against Tromso in their Conference League qualifier on Thursday.

Brighton manager Fabian Hurzeler was asked about Baleba during his pre-match press conference on Friday. "He's a Brighton player. Like I said, I'll never comment on any rumours that are currently in the media, it's also something I definitely can't control," the German said.

"A lot of things are written, I know about situations but again, in two days I have a very important game together with my team and with my staff. We want to have a good start in the Premier League season, that's the only focus we have at the moment."

‌



View 2 Images Manchester United are long-term admirers of Carlos Baleba (Image: Getty Images)

Carrick has been vocal about the need for new arrivals in midfield this summer following the departure of Casemiro and the long-term injury suffered by Manuel Ugarte.

"I just think we're looking to strengthen the squad," he said when asked about Baleba ahead of their Premier League opener against Hull this weekend. "We're certainly working towards that, making the most of the situation that we have and trying to improve things and trying to move forward.

Article continues below

"You know, I said the same thing to you last time. So yeah, certainly trying to make the most of the opportunities to finish the window stronger than we went into it. And I think we're in a good way to doing that so far."

Sports.title: Arsenal transfer 'proof' revealed live on Sky Sports in Julian Alvarez and Vinicius Jr claim
Sports.content:
Arsenal transfer 'proof' revealed live on Sky Sports in Julian Alvarez and Vinicius Jr claim

Arsenal's transfer for Vinicius Junior ended in disappointment for Gunners fans, but there has been an interesting revelation during a broadcast live on Sky Sports

View 3 Images Ian Wright said he has 'proof' Vinicius Jr was signing for Arsenal

Sky Sports pundit Ian Wright has claimed he has "proof" Vinicius Junior was set to move to Arsenal this summer. The Gunners were engaged in a high profile transfer pursuit of the Brazilian, which ended with the forward signing a new contract at Real Madrid.

‌



It was a fascinating saga for football fans which saw plenty of toing-and-froing during the negotiations. With Vinicius' move now not happening, Arsenal are now pursuing Atletico Madrid forward Julian Alvarez.

‌



However, as Wright briefly started speaking about the Argentinian, he insisted Vinicius was, at one stage, on his way to Arsenal, despite both Gary Neville and Jamie Carragher appearing unconvinced.

‌



FOLLOW OUR ARSENAL FB PAGE! Latest Gunners news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Neville asked a leading question about Vinicius to Wright at the start of Sky Sports pre-match coverage of their Premier League opener against Coventry City. After Neville said: "Who are they bringing in?" Wright replied: "This is what I am saying.

"They were talking about...I don't know if Alvarez is coming. Obviously, then went for Vini, I know that was happening, people laughed at me. You two laughed."

‌



After Carragher snapped back: "That was never happening" Wright then replied: "At some stage, Ill show you, I'll show you the proof."

View 3 Images Vini Jr remained at Real Madrid amid interest from Arsenal (Image: Antonio Villalba/Real Madrid via Getty Images)

Wright did not divulge what exactly his proof was in regards to Vinicius, at one stage of the saga, heading to Arsenal this summer. He signed a new six-year deal to remain at the Bernabeu instead of moving to north London.

‌



Vinicius Jr was the second big name attacker to snub Arsenal, after Morgan Rogers opted to move to Chelsea for £117m. The Gunners have now switched their focus to Alvarez, which is proving to be another drawn out transfer saga.

Atletico did not include him in their La Liga opener against Malaga, after Diego Simeone stated the World Cup winner was not in the right frame of mind to compete.

View 3 Images Mikel Arteta's Arsenal pursued a move for Vinicius Jr (Image: 2026 The Arsenal Football Club Plc)

‌



After Wright told Carragher and Neville about his transfer "proof" he then added: "That's where we're going. I don't think we need to change the way we are playing, I just think we need to bring in that calibre of player to force it home."

One new signing who is already exciting Arsenal fans is Greek winger Christos Tzolis. His arrival from Club Brugge took place somewhat under the radar, as Arsenal were in the middle of the Vinicius and Rogers transfer sagas.

Sports.title: Ezri Konsa recalls earning approval of Arsenal star after one-on-one session
Sports.content:
Ezri Konsa recalls earning approval of Arsenal star after one-on-one session

Ezri Konsa's defensive quality has previously been hailed by Bukayo Saka, with Arsenal now signing the England international from Aston Villa for over £50million

View 2 Images Ezri Konsa has completed his move to Arsenal

Ezri Konsa has completed his move to Arsenal which means he can team up with Bukayo Saka - who has been vocal in praising his compatriot as one of the best defenders out there.

‌



The Gunners have been in the market for defensive reinforcements and finally secured a deal with Aston Villa for Konsa, who joins for £51million. Arsenal are without the injured William Saliba and Konsa's quality and versatility means he can play across the backline.

‌



Those assets have helped him become a regular in the England picture and it was whilst on international duty that he left his mark on Saka. The duo chose to do extras together, leaving Konsa to try and defend against the Arsenal winger in a one-on-one situation.

‌



Saka was open about his admiration for Konsa, with his comments coming back in 2024, and Konsa was touched to hear praise from such a respected player.

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

Konsa recalled the incident: “I think it was a couple of years ago with England, we did some one-on-one sessions, me against him, and yeah, I gave him a good test. I take a lot of pride in defending, I love defending so to hear that praise from him is nice.”

‌



The England international will come into a defensive unit that includes the likes of Saliba, Gabriel, Jurrien Timber and Piero Hincapie. They are regarded among the best in Europe and last season kept 19 Premier League clean sheets as Arsenal finally ended their wait for title glory.

Arsenal's defensive quality was also key in them making the Champions League final and Konsa wants to compliment what they have at the Emirates.

View 2 Images Ezri Konsa and Bukayo Saka have been England team-mates for several years

‌



He told the club's website: “The chemistry they have, they all want to defend for each other, the love they have for defending, they love keeping the ball out of the net which is what you have to do as a defender. But I just love the way they are together. What they've built over the past few years has been special.”

Konsa's move means he joins the likes of Bruno Guimaraes and Christos Tzolis in moving to north London this summer. Mikel Arteta is also understood to be eyeing another attacking addition before the transfer window shuts.

Sports.title: 'A massive 10 days' - Neville tells Arsenal to get Alvarez before deadline
Sports.content:
Defending Premier League champions Arsenal would become Champions League winners if they land Julian Alvarez in the final days of the transfer window, says Gary Neville.

The Gunners have made an impressive start to the new campaign, backing up their Community Shield win over Manchester City with a 3-0 demolition of newly-promoted Coventry.

However, Sky Sports pundit Neville says Arsenal still need "a bit of magic up front" and believes Atletico Madrid's Alvarez is the player who would deliver it.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights from the Premier League match between Arsenal and Coventry

Arsenal, Barcelona and Paris Saint-Germain are among the clubs keen on Argentina international Alvarez, although Atletico CEO Miguel Angel Gil said earlier this summer that they do not want to sell Alvarez and would not even accept £170m for the forward.

Neville has encouraged Arsenal to test Atletico's resolve in a bid to take themselves to the next level.

"What a squad [Mikel Arteta] has built," said Neville. "If he puts another forward into that, if they could get Julian Alvarez somehow, that would light this place up as you'd have a world-class striker to go with all the world-class defenders and midfielders.

"They wouldn't just become Premier League title winners they'd go the next step and win a Champions League. It's a massive 10 days. He needs a bit of magic up front - someone that can win a game for you when you don't play well."

Speaking in his post-match press conference, Arteta insisted "the main focus has to be to improve our players and the connection between them". He noted how little Bukayo Saka, Martin Odegaard and Ben White played together down the right flank last season due to injuries.

However, Neville reckons Odegaard would be even more destructive if he had a striker like Alvarez to target.

"He [Odegaard] is exceptional. If there was an Ian Wright-type player up front for Arsenal who makes those short runs he'd be even better," said Neville.

Image: Arsenal's Martin Odegaard celebrates scoring his side's third goal against Coventry

"As [Kai] Havertz and [Viktor] Gyokeres always come to the ball, Odegaard has to play possession rather than playing the slip passes. If Arsenal were to sign Julian Alvarez then he'd go up a level as it would be perfect for the style of play."

Fellow Sky Sports pundit Jamie Carragher agreed Arsenal still need something special in the attacking areas, although he reckons Odegaard and Saka are showing signs of being able to reach world-class levels.

"I still think Arsenal lack a world-class player in the front four," he said. "About two years ago I thought Saka and Odegaard would make that next step. For whatever reason it's not happened due to injuries or Arsenal not being at their best. Those two were close to getting to the levels shown by Man City and Liverpool players, like [Kevin] De Bruyne and [Erling] Haaland or [Mohamed] Salah and [Sadio] Mane. They took their teams to the title.

"Arsenal won the league without [Saka and Odegaard] doing it. They did it by having a great defence and goalkeeper. But I still think Saka and Odegaard can get back to where they were a couple of years ago."

Carragher added: "The psychological factor of being champions now will take this Arsenal team to another level rather than buying a superstar player."

Analysis: Odegaard and Tzolis rejuvenate Arsenal attack

Sky Sports' Sam Blitz at the Emirates Stadium:

Vinicius Jr this, Morgan Rogers that... Arsenal have shown that their transfer window was better than many made out.

Tzolis looks like a gem, a real livewire down the left wing. After a stale opening five minutes on the pitch, he set it alight with two shots and two chances created in the space of four minutes.

It was no surprise to se him strongly involved in the two goals that put this game to bed, winning the ball high up for the first, then crossing for Saka for the second.

But Odegaard's start to the season cannot be overlooked either. He backed up the stunning Community Shield display with a first goal of the season here, equalling his league tally last season that saw him miss 30 matches in all competitions.

In fact, this was just the second time since December 2024 that Saka, Odegaard and Havertz had started together. All three scored against Coventry.

Odegaard is like a new signing. And with three open-play goals, Arsenal look like a new team.

Sports.title: Arsenal kick off title defence with thumping win over Coventry
Sports.content:
Arsenal made a flying start to their Premier League title defence with a 3-0 thumping of newly-promoted Coventry City in the season opener at the Emirates Stadium.

The Gunners showed their readiness to go again with an impressive demolition of Man City in the Community Shield last weekend and they sent another statement to their rivals for the crown with this demonstration of dominance.

Coventry's unwanted stat Coventry became the first team to have no touches in the opposition box or make a tackle in the first half of a Premier League game, since Opta started collecting that data in 2007.



They eventually made their first tackle on 69 minutes - when they were 3-0 down.

Once again new signing Christos Tzolis shone. The Greece international notched two assists at the Principality Stadium and was involved in Arsenal's first two goals on his Premier League debut, first winning the ball back for Riccardo Calafiori to tee up Kai Havertz and then sending in the cross Coventry 'keeper Carl Rushworth diverted into Bukayo Saka's path. "What a left-winger Arsenal have got," purred Sky Sports' Jamie Carragher on co-commentary.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Kai Havertz fires Arsenal in front against Coventry as the Gunners begin their title defence

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Bukayo Saka doubles Arsenal's lead

This was a reality check for Coventry on their return to the top flight after 25 years away. They failed to make a tackle in the first half - they could not get near Mikel Arteta's men. It did not get much better for them after the interval, with Martin Odegaard's miscued finish adding a third for Arsenal just four minutes into the second period.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Martin Odegaard nets the third for Arsenal

With Ben White, Saka and Odegaard combining brilliantly through the right channel, Tzolis electric on the left, and Havertz looking sharp ahead of some slick midfield play from Declan Rice and Myles Lewis-Skelly, Arsenal already look up to speed and formidable.

Where was Guimaraes? New Arsenal midfielder Bruno Guimaraes was missing with a thigh injury he picked up in the Community Shield win over Man City.

Their defence was barely tested but Ezri Konsa's pre-match welcome, following his £55m move from Aston Villa, was a reminder they have brought even greater strength and depth to that department, too. Tougher tests are to come, with Aston Villa away and Chelsea at home next on the fixture list, but Arsenal are going to take some stopping.

Coventry, meanwhile, will be relieved they do not have to face Arsenal again until April. They host Hull City next weekend in a fixture which will carry far more significance for their season.

The key moments from the Emirates

5: SHOT! Tzolis shoots over after cutting inside from the left flank.

7: OVER! Saka's shot is deflected over after Tzolis pops up on the right.

8: CLOSE! Tzolis is involved in everything Arsenal do in attack but sends his second shot of the game over after a well-worked short corner.

9: OVER! Declan Rice shoots over from 25 yards as Arsenal make a fast start.

15: GOAL! Tzolis wins the ball off Milan van Ewijk deep in Coventry territory, Calafiori crosses low for Havertz and the striker sweeps in a fine finish to give the Gunners the lead.

23: GOAL! Rice and Odegaard combine in midfield and Saka is perfectly placed to tuck in when Tzolis' cross is diverted into his path by Coventry 'keeper Rushworth.

Image: Havertz celebrates scoring the opening goal with Saka

34: CHANCE! Arsenal work the ball into the Coventry box and White is onto it but sees his shot blocked away. Coventry scrambling.

43: SHOT! Loum Tchaouna's overhead kick from the edge of the box loops onto the roof of the Arsenal net.

45+1: CLOSE! Rice whips a shot beyond the far post after another short corner.

49: GOAL! Odegaard, Saka and White combine through the right channel before the captain's miscued shot deceives Rushworth and adds Arsenal's third.

Image: Odegaard celebrates his goal

53: SAVE! Rushworth tips a curling effort from Lewis-Skelly over the bar for a corner as Arsenal keep their pedal to the metal.

66: SHOT! Tzolis stings Rushworth's palms with a drive from the edge of the box from an Arsenal corner.

90: SAVE! Rushworth is at full stretch to prevent Havertz arrowing in a fourth after some neat footwork from the Arsenal striker.

Arteta: A lot to like and big individual performances

Arsenal boss Mikel Arteta to Sky Sports:

"There was a lot to like. We were really dominant and flowed with the ball, connecting well with one another. We should have scored more goals.

150 PL wins up for Arteta Mikel Arteta recorded his 150th Premier League victory in charge of Arsenal, and is now one of only five managers to reach 150 wins in fewer than 250 games (249), after Pep Guardiola (204), Jose Mourinho (231), Jurgen Klopp (237), and Alex Ferguson (247).

"Overall the performance was positive with some big individual performances.

"When you talk about connection and chemistry those three [Saka, Odegaard and White] have that. They play so many minutes together in the past but they didn't play much last year due to different situations. Even on the left side with Tzolis you are seeing different dynamics. I was really impressed."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player The Friday Night Football panel discuss whether Arsenal are still shy of a world-class attacker that would see them get over the line to win their first UEFA Champions League title

Arsenal playing with swagger?

Sky Sports' Jamie Carragher:

"We'll know in a few weeks if there is a little bit of swagger about them or whether it was just the case they were playing against a team that were not used to that level. But Arsenal showed their class."

Odegaard: We can play even better!

Martin Odegaard speaking to Sky Sports:

"The first game is always a bit nervy. They played well, gave us a good fight and a good battle. Was key to get the first goal and control the game. It was solid.

"We looked good. We could have created and scored more. We can be more precise and sharp around the box. It's a good performance but we can do even better.

"The quality in the squad is unbelievable. You can put anyone on the pitch and they can perform at the highest level. We push one another to get better."

Lampard: A big learning curve

Coventry boss Frank Lampard:

"I didn't mind the reaction towards the end of the game as we went on. I saw some okay things there. It was a big learning curve, I believe they kept going, they kept going much to the end.

"There's Premier League debuts, there's noise here, I remember that [as a player]. It's different to the Championship in a way, no matter where you go.

"So those things are things to handle as a player, and we talked about a lot before the game. They'll have to go through that and experience that."

YOUR VIEWS: Coventry concerns and encouraging signs for Arsenal

Sheldon: Quality of Tzolis!! I know it's a first game back but if he continues like that £34m looks like a bargain, great first performance from the champions COYG!!

Reeze: Arsenal will walk the league this year, even without adding another forward. Problem is, they probably will add another!

Craig: Arsenal looked good and comfortable and never really had to break sweat but I thought Coventry were very, very poor, the goalkeeper has thrown one in and gifted them another. Tonight won't define their season but they are going to have to be much, much better.

Combo: Arsenal played well but Coventry don't look great so it's hard to judge it. We got the goals at decent times and controlled basically everything in the game. Probably could have gotten more but good start to the season. And for Coventry, it will be a real battle this season.

Luca Hill: Tzolis is Arsenal's Kvaratskhelia. A new, underestimated, diamond to the crown.

Sports.title: Wigan top Super League table with win over Wakefield as Leigh rout Bradford
Sports.content:
Wigan eased to the top of the Betfred Super League table with a club-record 12th straight win after seeing off gutsy Wakefield 26-12 at the Brick Community Stadium.

Matt Peet's men brutally exploited a series of handling errors by the visitors to muscle into a 20-point half-time lead, then repelled a fine fightback with Jai Field's length-of-field interception just past the hour mark to seal their win.

The manner and timing of their move into pole position looks ominous for their top-flight rivals, not least long-time leaders Leeds who are now under pressure when they head to York on Sunday.

Peet praised his side's tenacity, saying: "I'm very pleased with how the game unfolded. The first half was intense and went set for set for a long time and we came out the other side of that.

"In the second half we got a little bit sloppy but we had to defend for the most part and it probably did us good. Wakefield throw so much threat at you and they never stop asking questions."

It marked a fourth straight loss for Wakefield, who started well and were aggrieved to be denied the opening try when Oliver Pratt sent Max Jowitt sliding over, but he was ruled to have knocked on in the process of grounding.

Moments earlier, Wakefield rode their luck to stay level after a rare error from Bevan French, who sent Zach Eckersley over in the corner from a forward pass.

Luke Thompson came close for Wigan while Wakefield continued to benefit on the short side as a high-quality contest moved past the quarter-hour without a point on the board.

But Wigan proceeded to capitalise on a pair of Wakefield errors to run in three tries in the next 10 minutes and give themselves an almost insurmountable advantage.

French ruthlessly punished a careless pass by Jowitt by powering over the halfway line to open the scoring, and six minutes later Wigan built on a penalty pass with Kian McDermott's superb ball gifting Liam Marshall the second in the corner.

Marshall was in for his second almost immediately after another handling error gifted Wigan the advantage. Three kicks from Adam Keighran - coupled with a penalty on the hooter - sent Peet's men in at the interval four scores to the good.

Wakefield might have been all but resigned to another defeat but they will take great heart from the way they refused to accept the seemingly inevitable at the start of the second half.

They seized on a sustained spell of pressure to narrow the deficit on 52 minutes when Jake Trueman's clever kick eluded French and gave Corey Hall the chance to touch down.

Trinity pushed again on the back of a penalty and a repeat set, and could have further reduced the deficit but for Hall's foot straying into touch as he flicked the ball back for Jowitt to go over.

The visitors' hopes were finally dashed when a spill from Mike McMeeken sent Jai Field scurrying the length of the field to score Wigan's fourth. A late effort from Wakefield's Ky Rodwell made the final scoreline more respectable.

Wakefield head coach Daryl Powell criticised the officials, saying: "I do think the refereeing department have to ask themselves a couple of questions.

"There's two teams that were top class but there's other parts of the game that weren't. I'll be asking my team to get better from tonight and I think [the officials] should be doing the same."

Leopards continue play-off charge with emphatic rout

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights of Leigh Leopards against Bradford Bulls in the Super League

Leigh Leopards continued their charge for the play-offs with a 62-10 thumping of Bradford Bulls.

Adam Cook scored 30 points, slotting over all 11 kicks and crossing for two tries, with Leigh adding 48 points in a one-sided second half.

Robbie Mulhern scored the first try for the hosts in the 12th minute, with Cook adding the conversion and a penalty before poor handling by the Leopards led to Waqa Blake powering over in the corner for Bradford.

Louis Brogan ended a spell of Leigh pressure by scoring their second try to make it 14-4 at the break, and the tone for the second half was set from the opening moment.

Bradford fumbled the kick-off, allowing Innes Senior to go over in the corner, and the tries arrived thick and fast for the hosts.

Lachlan Lam started and finished a move in the 48th minute before playing in Cook, who chased down his own kick.

Senior then grabbed his second, Umyla Hanley finished off Lam's brilliant long pass and Joe Ofahengaue completed a flowing move with more than 10 minutes still remaining.

Cook then broke away for his second try and Lam finished off a brilliant individual performance with his second, although the final word went to Bradford and Eliot Peposhi.

Sports.title: Hunt follows European heroics with 200m silver in Diamond League
Sports.content:
Britain's Amy Hunt travelled to Switzerland on the back of winning four gold medals at the European Championships

Amy Hunt followed up her historic European Championships performance by finishing second in the 200 metres at the Lausanne Diamond League.

Less than a week after completing her set of four gold medals in Birmingham, the sprinter was on the starting blocks in Switzerland and she edged out Nigerian Favour Ofili in a photo finish.

Hunt's time of 22.32sec was some way off American winner Kayla White's 22.18, while two-time world champion Shericka Jackson failed to finish after suffering a leg injury.

Zharnel Hughes finished fifth in the equivalent men's race, which was won by Botswana's Olympic champion Letsile Tebogo, while Elise Thorner was eighth in the women's 3,000m steeplechase.

The most popular winner of the night, meanwhile, was home favourite Audrey Werro, who, just a week after beating Britain's Keely Hodgkinson to European 800m gold, triumphed again.

Werro pipped Dutchwoman Femke Bol, while the former 400m hurdler continued her rapid rise by setting a new national record of 1:55.41.

"The turnaround after the European Championships was very short, so I had to recover quickly, and I felt more tired than ​usual today," Werro said. "Despite that, I managed to win, so I'm very happy."

Olympic champion Masai Russell of the ⁠US led from the first barrier to win the women's 100m hurdles ​in 12.27 for her ninth consecutive victory this season.

"It was another win, so it keeps the streak alive, and ​I'm very pleased," Russell said. "I hadn't raced in a month, so I was really happy to see that my performance was right where I left it."

Sports.title: McIlroy heads back to range after slipping off BMW Championship pace
Sports.content:
Rory McIlroy was heading straight to the driving range after slipping off the pace during round two of the BMW Championship in St Louis.

The Masters champion began with a fine six-under-par opening round for a share of the lead, but could only improve his total by one shot on Friday with a 69.

"I feel like conditions were pretty similar to yesterday," McIlroy told the Golf Channel.

"The wind was coming out of a different direction, but still very scorable. The greens are soft, maybe the ball's got a little bit more run out on the fairways, but you'll still see guys shooting pretty good scores today.

"I didn't quite hit it as good as I did yesterday, so probably an afternoon on the range for me.

"I'm proud of how I just hung in there. A lot of good par putts on the back nine, especially. The only bogey I had was with a mistake on the par-five eighth hole, but I made some really good par saves coming in and that sort of kept me in it."

Speaking about the fans at Bellerive, six-time major champion McIlroy added: "They're amazing, that's one of the biggest things I remember from being here in 2018 for the PGA was just how many people showed up and what a great atmosphere it was to play in.

"Yesterday was amazing for a Thursday. Today, teeing off at 9:45 on a Friday morning and the people out there were incredible. Looking forward to more of the same over the weekend."

Image: Wyndham Clark leads by one shot

Two-time US Open champion Wyndham Clark, the only player in the field yet to drop a shot, leads the way on 12 under after back-to-back 64s.

Gary Woodland is a shot behind while a third American, JJ Spaun, looked set to run away with the second round after he moved to 11 under at the turn.

Three bogeys on the back nine checked his progress but two birdies, including one at the last, left him as clubhouse leader of the early starters on 10 under.

World No 1 Scottie Scheffler, who was two over after a first-round 72, bogeyed the first hole but recovered well after the turn with five birdies leaving him still in contention - albeit in joint 25th - at three under.

Sports.title: Man Utd agree £70m deal for Baleba
Sports.content:
Manchester United have agreed a £70m deal for Brighton midfielder Carlos Baleba.

The deal is worth £65m guaranteed, plus £5m in add-ons, and Brighton have also inserted a sell-on clause.

Baleba is expected to sign a five-year-contract with Manchester United and will undergo his medical in the next 24 hours.

Sky Sports News has been reporting on United's interest in Baleba since last autumn and broke the news that they had enquired about signing him during the January transfer window.

He remained one of United's top targets this summer and will become their third addition in midfield after Andrey Santos and Youri Tielemans.

One source has told Sky Sports News when United looked to pursue Baleba last summer - they were quoted an initial price higher than the fee Moises Caicedo cost when he joined Chelsea in 2023, which was £100m, plus £15m in performance-related add-ons.

Despite Baleba's undoubted dip in form for Brighton last season, officials at United are understood to be happy with the deal 12 months on as they have had a long-standing interest in the player.

When will Baleba make United debut?

Baleba is recovering from an ankle ligament injury he picked up during pre-season and Sky Sports News understands he is due to be fit around the middle of September.

Manchester United face Manchester City on September 13 and Fulham on September 20, followed by the three-week international break which will allow Baleba ample time to acclimatise to life at Old Trafford.
